- gold notes: @abbeyskitchen on the BBC World Service report into Steven Bartlett's Diary of a CEO podcast. Structurally unusual and useful for the stance step: the video opens cold on a clip of someone else's claims, with no framing until several seconds later, so a system reading only the first lines would see vaccine-autism and anti-COVID-vaccine assertions presented flat. The framing that makes it REFUTES arrives afterwards. All three refuted claims are contradicted by retrievable evidence, so DEBUNKING rests on solid ground. The claims about what the BBC report found are claims about a document rather than health assertions, so they are not rows. This collector's folder carried no label.

- gold notes: Dr. Rubin taking apart a viral 'things they told us were unhealthy' video point by point, and explaining the technique as he goes: flash a citation too briefly to read, take a kernel of truth, shroud it in things out of context. The salt segment is the best-documented example in the bundle of citation misuse -- he names the PURE study, the journal and the year, and then explains why spot urine sodium samples cannot carry the conclusion drawn from them. That is a methodological critique, not a contradiction, so the refuted claim lands on MIXED and the video comes out CANNOT_RECOGNIZE rather than DEBUNKING. Under the revised section 9 it now goes to review as a possible debunk of an unsettled claim, which is the outcome that rule was written for. Collectors filed it under DEBUNKING.

- gold notes: An alternative-medicine framing of heart attacks as clotting events rather than plaque events, then a list of clot triggers and ways to raise nitric oxide. The most mixed video in the set: the framing claim overreaches, several of the risk-factor claims are solidly supported, and the '2,000%' bereavement figure turns out to match a real study almost exactly -- which is why it is worth having. Comes out NO_MISINFO because the overreaching framing lands on MIXED rather than CONTRADICTED. In the blind subset. This collector's folder carried no label.
